prompt: Rising sea levels ___ a serious threat to coastal cities such as Venice.

explanation.rule: La colocación fija es 'pose a threat' (suponer/representar una amenaza).

wrong.make: 'make a threat' significa amenazar verbalmente a alguien (he made threats against his boss); el mar no 'amenaza' así, supone un peligro.
wrong.give: 'give a threat' no es una colocación en inglés.
wrong.do: 'do a threat' no existe; en inglés 'threat' no va con 'do'.

examples: Air pollution poses a risk to public health.
The new virus poses no threat to humans.

prompt: The team worked all weekend to ___ the deadline for the grant application.

explanation.rule: Con 'deadline' se dice 'meet a deadline' (cumplir un plazo); lo contrario es 'miss a deadline'.

wrong.reach: 'reach' se usa con 'an agreement' o 'a goal', no con 'deadline'.
wrong.fulfil: 'fulfil' va con 'a requirement', 'a promise' o 'a dream', no con 'deadline'.
wrong.arrive: 'arrive' es intransitivo: no puede llevar objeto directo ('arrive the deadline' es incorrecto).

examples: If we don't meet the deadline, we'll lose the contract.
She has never missed a deadline.

prompt: As head of department, you ___ full responsibility for the safety of your staff.

explanation.rule: 'Bear responsibility' (cargar con / asumir la responsabilidad) es una colocación formal habitual.

wrong.support: Calco de 'soportar'; 'support' significa apoyar, no cargar con una responsabilidad.
wrong.wear: 'wear' es llevar puesto (ropa, gafas); no se usa con 'responsibility'.
wrong.suffer: 'suffer' es sufrir (un dolor, una pérdida); no se 'sufre' una responsabilidad en inglés.

examples: Parents bear responsibility for their children's education.
Nobody wanted to bear the blame for the mistake.

prompt: From the results of the survey, we can ___ the conclusion that most customers prefer shopping online.

explanation.rule: En inglés se dice 'draw a conclusion' (sacar una conclusión).

wrong.take: Calco de 'sacar/tomar una conclusión'; 'take a conclusion' no es natural en inglés.
wrong.extract: Calco de 'extraer'; 'extract' se usa con datos o información, no con 'conclusion'.
wrong.pull: 'pull' es tirar de algo físicamente; no forma colocación con 'conclusion'.

examples: It's too early to draw any conclusions.
What conclusions can we draw from these figures?

prompt: After six hours of discussion, the committee finally ___ a consensus on the new budget.

explanation.rule: Con 'consensus' (y 'agreement') se usa 'reach': reach a consensus (llegar a un consenso).

wrong.arrived: 'arrive' necesita la preposición 'at' (arrive at a consensus); sin 'at' es incorrecto.
wrong.hit: 'hit' se usa con 'a target' o 'a record', no con 'consensus'.
wrong.touched: 'touch' es tocar físicamente; no forma colocación con 'consensus'.

examples: The two parties failed to reach a consensus.
We reached an agreement after long negotiations.

prompt: Which expression means 'un aumento brusco' in English?

explanation.rule: 'A sharp increase/rise/fall' describe un cambio brusco y repentino.

wrong.a hard increase: 'hard' no se combina con 'increase'; sería un calco de 'duro'.
wrong.a tall increase: 'tall' describe altura de personas, árboles o edificios, no cifras.

examples: There has been a sharp increase in house prices.
Sales fell sharply in March.

prompt: The new evidence ___ serious doubt on the official version of events.

explanation.rule: 'Cast doubt on something' significa poner en duda algo.

wrong.puts: Calco de 'poner en duda'; 'put doubt on' no es la colocación inglesa.
wrong.launches: Calco de 'lanzar dudas'; 'launch' se usa con campañas o productos.
wrong.drops: 'drop' es dejar caer; no forma colocación con 'doubt'.

examples: The report casts doubt on the minister's claims.
Recent studies have cast doubt on this theory.

prompt: Her research has ___ a major contribution to our understanding of the disease.

explanation.rule: Se dice 'make a contribution (to something)': hacer una aportación.

wrong.done: 'do' no se combina con 'contribution'; con 'contribution' el verbo es 'make'.
wrong.brought: Calco de 'aportar'; 'bring a contribution' no es natural en inglés.
wrong.given: 'give a contribution' se usa a veces para donaciones de dinero, pero no para aportaciones a la ciencia.

examples: Each member of the team made a valuable contribution.
Immigrants have made a huge contribution to the economy.

prompt: Which verb specifically means 'to say that someone has done something wrong or illegal, without giving proof'?

explanation.rule: 'Allege' = afirmar que alguien ha hecho algo malo o ilegal sin haberlo probado (de ahí 'alleged', presunto).

wrong.claim: 'claim' es afirmar algo que puede no ser cierto, pero no implica necesariamente acusar de algo ilegal.
wrong.assert: 'assert' es afirmar con firmeza y seguridad, sin idea de acusación.
wrong.state: 'state' es declarar algo de forma clara y oficial; es neutro, no acusa a nadie.

examples: She alleged that her manager had stolen the money.
The alleged thief was arrested this morning.

prompt: What does 'assert' mean in: 'She asserted her right to speak at the meeting'?

explanation.rule: 'Assert' significa afirmar con firmeza o hacer valer (un derecho, la autoridad).

wrong.acertar: Falso amigo por el parecido de sonido; 'acertar' es 'get it right' o 'guess correctly'.
wrong.aceptar: 'aceptar' es 'accept'; 'assert her right' es reclamarlo, no aceptarlo.

examples: He asserted that he was innocent.
You need to assert yourself more in meetings.

prompt: Three passengers were seriously ___ in the crash, but fortunately nobody died.

explanation.rule: 'Injure' se usa para heridas físicas de personas o animales en accidentes; 'damage' para cosas.

wrong.damaged: 'damage' se usa con objetos (a car, a building), no con personas.
wrong.broken: 'broken' se usa para huesos u objetos (a broken leg), no para personas enteras.
wrong.spoiled: 'spoil' es estropear (comida, planes) o mimar a un niño; no se refiere a heridas.

examples: She injured her back lifting boxes.
Two people were injured in the fire.

prompt: The storm ___ the roof of the school, so classes were cancelled for a week.

explanation.rule: 'Damage' = dañar cosas materiales (edificios, coches, objetos).

wrong.injured: 'injure' es herir a personas o animales, no a un tejado.
wrong.hurt: 'hurt' es hacer daño a personas (física o emocionalmente), no a objetos.
wrong.wounded: 'wound' es herir con un arma (bala, cuchillo); solo se usa con personas.

examples: The earthquake damaged hundreds of buildings.
Smoking can damage your lungs.

prompt: Too much screen time can do children more ___ than good.

explanation.rule: La expresión fija es 'do more harm than good' (hacer más mal que bien); 'harm' es daño en sentido general.

wrong.bad: Calco de 'más mal que bien'; en inglés 'bad' no se usa como sustantivo en esta expresión: se dice 'more harm than good'.
wrong.injury: 'injury' es una lesión física concreta; no encaja en esta expresión.
wrong.hurt: 'hurt' como sustantivo significa dolor emocional; la expresión fija usa 'harm'.

examples: A little sunshine won't do you any harm.
Strict diets often do more harm than good.

prompt: In the thick fog, we could barely ___ the outline of the lighthouse.

explanation.rule: 'Discern' (formal) = distinguir o percibir algo con dificultad.

wrong.warn: 'warn' es advertir de un peligro a alguien; no significa ver o distinguir.
wrong.realise: 'realise' es darse cuenta de un hecho (realise that...), no distinguir algo con la vista.
wrong.advert: Calco de 'advertir'; 'advert' en inglés es un anuncio publicitario (sustantivo).

examples: I could just discern a figure in the distance.
It is difficult to discern any pattern in the data.

prompt: Many people ___ the new law as an attack on their personal freedom.

explanation.rule: 'Perceive something as...' = ver/interpretar algo de cierta manera.

wrong.notice: 'notice' es fijarse en algo; no se usa con la estructura 'notice X as Y'.
wrong.realise: 'realise' es darse cuenta de algo; no admite 'realise X as Y'.
wrong.discern: 'discern' es distinguir algo difícil de ver o entender; no se usa con 'as' para dar una interpretación.

examples: She is perceived as a strong leader.
How do you think others perceive you?

prompt: The scientists designed an experiment to test their ___ that the drug reduces memory loss.

explanation.rule: 'Hypothesis' (plural 'hypotheses') = hipótesis, una idea que se comprueba con experimentos.

wrong.hypothetical: 'hypothetical' es un adjetivo (hipotético); después de 'their' necesitamos un sustantivo.
wrong.suppose: 'suppose' es un verbo (suponer), no puede ir después de 'their'.
wrong.proof: 'proof' es una prueba que ya demuestra algo; no tiene sentido 'testear' una prueba antes de hacer el experimento.

examples: The results support our original hypothesis.
Scientists have proposed several hypotheses.

prompt: The report provides a ___ analysis of the housing market, covering every region of the country.

explanation.rule: 'Comprehensive' = completo, exhaustivo. No significa 'comprensivo' (eso es 'understanding').

wrong.comprehensible: 'comprehensible' = que se puede entender; no expresa que el análisis cubra todo.
wrong.understanding: 'understanding' = comprensivo con los demás; se dice de personas, no de un análisis.
wrong.comprehending: 'comprehending' es el gerundio de 'comprehend' (entender); no funciona como adjetivo aquí.

examples: We offer comprehensive insurance for your car.
The book is a comprehensive guide to Spanish history.

prompt: Constant criticism from his boss slowly ___ his confidence until he decided to resign.

explanation.rule: 'Undermine' = socavar, debilitar algo poco a poco (confianza, autoridad, esfuerzos).

wrong.underlined: 'underline' es subrayar (un texto o una idea), no debilitar.
wrong.underwent: 'undergo' es someterse a algo (an operation, changes); no lleva 'his confidence' como objeto con este sentido.
wrong.underestimated: 'underestimate' es subestimar; la crítica no 'subestima' la confianza de nadie.

examples: These rumours could undermine the company's reputation.
Lack of sleep undermines your ability to concentrate.

prompt: The government has created a legal ___ to protect personal data online.

explanation.rule: 'Framework' = marco (estructura de reglas o ideas): a legal framework, a theoretical framework.

wrong.mark: Calco de 'marco'; 'mark' es una marca o una nota escolar.
wrong.frame: 'frame' es el marco físico de un cuadro o una ventana, no un marco legal o teórico.
wrong.picture: 'picture' es una imagen o un cuadro; no expresa un conjunto de normas.

examples: The study uses a clear theoretical framework.
We need a framework for international cooperation.

prompt: The study found a ___ link between lack of sleep and poor memory.

explanation.rule: 'Significant' = importante, considerable o estadísticamente relevante; es el adjetivo que va delante de un sustantivo.

wrong.signifying: 'signifying' es el gerundio de 'signify' (significar); no describe el vínculo.
wrong.significance: 'significance' es el sustantivo (importancia); delante de 'link' hace falta un adjetivo.
wrong.signified: 'signified' es el participio de 'signify'; 'a signified link' no tiene sentido.

examples: There was a significant rise in prices.
The difference between the two groups was not significant.

prompt: What does 'empirical evidence' mean?
options: pruebas basadas en la observación o la experimentación

explanation.rule: 'Empirical' = basado en la observación o la experiencia, no solo en la teoría.

wrong.pruebas teóricas sin datos: Es justo lo contrario: 'empirical' se opone a 'theoretical'.
wrong.pruebas de origen imperial: 'empirical' no tiene relación con 'empire' (imperio), aunque se parezcan.
wrong.pruebas falsas o inventadas: 'empirical' no implica falsedad; al contrario, se basa en datos reales.

examples: There is little empirical evidence to support this claim.
The theory was tested in an empirical study.

prompt: What does 'casualties' mean in: 'The earthquake caused hundreds of casualties'?

explanation.rule: 'Casualty' = víctima (muerto o herido) en un accidente, guerra o desastre; 'casualidad' es 'coincidence' o 'chance'.

wrong.casualidades: Falso amigo: 'casualidad' en inglés es 'coincidence' o 'chance'.
wrong.accidentes sin importancia: 'casualties' son personas, no accidentes; y no son nada leves.

examples: There were no casualties in the fire.
He was taken to the casualty department of the hospital.

prompt: What does 'eventual' mean in: 'Despite a bad start, she was the eventual winner of the tournament'?

explanation.rule: 'Eventual' = final, el que resulta al final de un proceso. 'Eventual' en español (posible) es 'possible'.

wrong.posible: Falso amigo: el 'eventual' español (posible) se dice 'possible' o 'potential'.

examples: The eventual cost of the project was twice the original estimate.
After many delays, they eventually arrived at midnight.

prompt: What does 'contest' mean in: 'His family plans to contest the will in court'?

explanation.rule: Como verbo, 'contest' = impugnar o disputar (una decisión, un resultado, un testamento). 'Contestar' es 'answer' o 'reply'.

wrong.contestar, responder: Falso amigo: 'contestar' en inglés es 'answer' o 'reply'.
wrong.participar en un concurso: 'contest' como sustantivo es un concurso, pero aquí es un verbo con objeto ('the will').
wrong.confesar: 'confesar' es 'confess'; no se parece en significado.

examples: The opposition contested the election results.
She decided not to contest the fine.

prompt: Please be ___: don't tell anyone in the office about my new job yet.

explanation.rule: 'Discreet' = discreto, reservado (que no cuenta secretos). 'Discrete' = separado, independiente.

wrong.discrete: 'discrete' (con -te) significa separado o diferenciado, no reservado.
wrong.discretion: 'discretion' es el sustantivo (discreción); después de 'be' hace falta un adjetivo.
wrong.indiscreet: 'indiscreet' es lo contrario: alguien que cuenta lo que debería callar.

examples: He was very discreet about his private life.
Can I count on your discretion?

prompt: The course is divided into five ___ units that can be studied in any order.

explanation.rule: 'Discrete' (formal/académico) = separado, independiente, diferenciado.

wrong.discreet: 'discreet' (con -eet) es reservado, prudente; se dice de personas, no de unidades de un curso.
wrong.humble: 'humble' es humilde; no indica que las unidades sean independientes.
wrong.modest: 'modest' es modesto o pequeño; no explica que se puedan estudiar en cualquier orden.

examples: The process can be broken down into discrete stages.
Light behaves like discrete particles.

prompt: In a research paper, what is the 'abstract'?
options: el resumen breve al principio del artículo
una parte abstracta y difícil de entender

explanation.rule: En textos académicos, 'abstract' = resumen breve del artículo que aparece al principio.

wrong.una parte abstracta y difícil de entende: Aunque 'abstract' también es el adjetivo 'abstracto', como sustantivo en un artículo es el resumen.

examples: The abstract should be no longer than 250 words.
Read the abstract first to see if the paper is relevant.

prompt: What does 'consistent' mean in: 'His story was not consistent with the evidence'?

explanation.rule: 'Consistent with' = coherente con, que concuerda con. Para 'consistente' (sólido, espeso) se dice 'solid', 'thick' o 'substantial'.

wrong.consistente, espeso: Falso amigo: una salsa 'consistente' es 'thick', no 'consistent'.
wrong.resistente, sólido: 'sólido' es 'solid' o 'sturdy'; 'consistent' no describe la resistencia.
wrong.constante en el tiempo: 'consistent' puede significar regular (a consistent player), pero con 'with the evidence' significa que concuerda.

examples: The results are consistent with previous studies.
She has been a consistent performer all season.

prompt: What does 'contemplate' mean in: 'The company is contemplating moving its headquarters to Madrid'?

explanation.rule: 'Contemplate + -ing' = plantearse, considerar la posibilidad de hacer algo.

wrong.mirar algo con admiración: 'contemplate' puede significar mirar con calma, pero con '+ -ing' (contemplating moving) significa plantearse.

examples: I would never contemplate leaving my family.
She is contemplating a career change.

prompt: The doctor ___ me that the medicine might make me feel sleepy.

explanation.rule: 'Warn someone that...' = advertir/avisar. 'Prevent' = impedir o evitar, no 'prevenir' en el sentido de avisar.

wrong.prevented: Falso amigo: 'prevenir' en el sentido de avisar es 'warn'; 'prevent' es impedir (prevent an accident).
wrong.noticed: Calco de 'notificar'; 'notice' es fijarse o darse cuenta, no avisar a alguien.
wrong.avoided: 'avoid' es evitar; 'avoided me that' es incorrecto.

examples: They warned us not to swim in the river.
Vaccines help prevent serious diseases.

prompt: After several accidents, the government plans to ___ the safety rules for building sites.

explanation.rule: El sufijo -en convierte adjetivos o sustantivos en verbos: strong → strengthen (reforzar), wide → widen, short → shorten.

wrong.strength: 'strength' es el sustantivo (fuerza); después de 'to' hace falta un verbo.
wrong.strong: 'strong' es el adjetivo; no puede funcionar como verbo.
wrong.strongly: 'strongly' es el adverbio; después de 'to' hace falta un verbo.

examples: The bridge needs to be strengthened.
They widened the road last year.

prompt: Supermarkets are trying to ___ the use of plastic bags by charging for them.

explanation.rule: El sufijo -ise (-ize en EE. UU.) forma verbos: minimum → minimise (reducir al mínimo).

wrong.minimum: 'minimum' es un sustantivo o adjetivo; después de 'to' necesitamos un verbo.
wrong.minimal: 'minimal' es adjetivo (mínimo); no puede ser el verbo.
wrong.minimally: 'minimally' es adverbio; no puede llevar 'the use' como objeto.

examples: We must minimise the risks.
The company wants to modernise its offices.

prompt: Could you ___ what you mean by 'flexible hours'? I'm not sure I understand.

explanation.rule: El sufijo -ify forma verbos: clear → clarify (aclarar), simple → simplify, just → justify.

wrong.clear: 'clear' como verbo es despejar o vaciar (clear the table); no se usa para aclarar lo que quieres decir.
wrong.clarity: 'clarity' es el sustantivo (claridad); después de 'Could you' hace falta un verbo.
wrong.clearance: 'clearance' es un sustantivo (autorización, liquidación); no es un verbo.

examples: Let me clarify the main points.
We need to simplify the application process.

prompt: The new vaccine has proved highly ___ against the virus.

explanation.rule: El sufijo -ive forma adjetivos: effect → effective (eficaz). 'Effective against' = eficaz contra.

wrong.affective: 'affective' es un término técnico de psicología (afectivo, emocional); no significa eficaz.
wrong.efficacy: 'efficacy' es el sustantivo (eficacia); después de 'highly' hace falta un adjetivo.
wrong.effected: 'effected' es el participio de 'effect' (llevar a cabo, formal); no describe la vacuna.

examples: This is the most effective treatment available.
Exercise is an effective way to reduce stress.

prompt: The film received ___ praise from critics: every single review was positive.

explanation.rule: El sufijo -ous forma adjetivos: unanimity → unanimous (unánime), fame → famous, danger → dangerous.

wrong.unanimity: 'unanimity' es el sustantivo (unanimidad); delante de 'praise' hace falta un adjetivo.
wrong.unanimously: 'unanimously' es el adverbio; modifica verbos (they voted unanimously), no sustantivos.

examples: The decision was unanimous.
The board voted unanimously in favour.

prompt: The instructions were so badly written that they were almost ___.

explanation.rule: Muchos adjetivos en -ible toman el prefijo in-: comprehensible → incomprehensible (incomprensible).

wrong.uncomprehensible: Con este adjetivo el prefijo negativo es 'in-', no 'un-'; 'uncomprehensible' no existe.
wrong.incomprehensive: 'comprehensive' significa completo; 'incomprehensive' no es una palabra estándar y no significa incomprensible.
wrong.incomprehension: 'incomprehension' es el sustantivo; después de 'were almost' hace falta un adjetivo.

examples: His accent was almost incomprehensible to me.
The handwriting was completely illegible.

prompt: I'm writing ___ behalf of my manager, who is currently on holiday.

explanation.rule: 'On behalf of someone' = en nombre de alguien / en representación de alguien.

wrong.by: 'by behalf of' no existe; la expresión siempre es 'on behalf of'.
wrong.for: 'for behalf of' es un error frecuente; la preposición fija es 'on'.
wrong.at: 'at behalf of' no existe en inglés.

examples: On behalf of everyone here, thank you.
She accepted the award on behalf of her father.

prompt: With regard ___ your recent enquiry, I am pleased to confirm that the room is available.

explanation.rule: 'With regard to' (formal) = en relación con, con respecto a.

wrong.of: Calco de 'con respecto de'; 'with regard of' es incorrecto.
wrong.at: 'at' no se combina con 'regard' en esta expresión.
wrong.about: 'about' sola ya significa 'sobre', pero 'with regard about' no existe.

examples: With regard to your complaint, we have refunded the full amount.
I have nothing to say with regard to that matter.

prompt: ___ the light of the new evidence, the court decided to reopen the case.

explanation.rule: 'In the light of' (también 'in light of' en EE. UU.) = a la luz de, teniendo en cuenta.

wrong.Under: 'under the light' es literalmente 'bajo la luz' (una lámpara); no es la expresión.
wrong.With: 'with the light of' no es una expresión fija en inglés.
wrong.At: Calco de 'a la luz de'; en inglés la preposición es 'in', no 'at'.

examples: In the light of recent events, the concert has been cancelled.
In light of the results, we will change our strategy.

prompt: Who is ___ charge of the marketing department while Laura is away?

explanation.rule: 'Be in charge of something' = estar a cargo de algo, ser el responsable.

wrong.at: Calco de 'a cargo de'; en inglés es 'in charge of', no 'at charge of'.
wrong.of: 'of' ya aparece después de 'charge'; delante hace falta 'in'.
wrong.on: 'on charge' no es la expresión; 'on a charge of' se usa para acusaciones (arrested on a charge of theft).

examples: Who's in charge here?
She was put in charge of the new project.

prompt: The decision was taken ___ accordance with the company's safety regulations.

explanation.rule: 'In accordance with' (formal) = de acuerdo con, conforme a.

wrong.with: 'with' va después de 'accordance', no antes: in accordance with.
wrong.of: Calco de 'de acuerdo con'; 'of accordance with' es incorrecto.
wrong.on: 'on accordance' no existe; la expresión fija empieza con 'in'.

examples: All waste must be disposed of in accordance with the law.
We acted in accordance with your instructions.

prompt: The conference will ___ at 9 a.m. with a welcome speech from the director.

explanation.rule: 'Commence' es el equivalente formal de 'start' o 'begin' y puede usarse sin objeto.

wrong.inaugurate: 'inaugurate' necesita objeto (inaugurate a building); 'the conference will inaugurate' no tiene sentido.
wrong.initiate: 'initiate' necesita objeto (initiate talks); no se usa solo con el sentido de empezar.
wrong.comment: 'comment' es comentar; se parece en la forma pero no tiene que ver.

examples: The ceremony will commence at noon.
Work commenced on the new bridge in May.

prompt: Formal notice: 'Tickets may be ___ online or at the box office.' Which verb fits?

explanation.rule: 'Purchase' es el equivalente formal de 'buy' (comprar).

wrong.shopped: 'shop' es intransitivo (go shopping); no se dice 'tickets may be shopped'.
wrong.acquainted: 'acquainted' significa familiarizado o conocido (be acquainted with someone).
wrong.adquired: Calco de 'adquirir'; la palabra inglesa es 'acquire' (y con c), y además no es lo habitual para entradas.

examples: Proof of purchase is required for all refunds.
The museum purchased the painting in 1998.

prompt: Dear customer, we will ___ to answer all enquiries within 48 hours.

explanation.rule: 'Endeavour to do something' (formal) = esforzarse por / procurar hacer algo.

wrong.procure: Calco de 'procurar'; 'procure' en inglés es conseguir u obtener algo, no intentar.
wrong.intent: 'intent' es un sustantivo o adjetivo; el verbo sería 'intend', y aun así cambiaría el sentido.

examples: We will endeavour to resolve the problem as soon as possible.
Every endeavour was made to find the missing child.

prompt: What does 'ascertain' mean in: 'The police are trying to ascertain the cause of the fire'?

explanation.rule: 'Ascertain' (formal) = averiguar o establecer algo con certeza; equivale a 'find out'.

wrong.acertar por casualidad: Falso amigo por el sonido; 'acertar' es 'get it right' o 'guess correctly'.

examples: We need to ascertain whether the information is accurate.
It was difficult to ascertain the truth.

prompt: After the 25-kilometre hike in the mountains, we were ___ exhausted.

explanation.rule: Los adjetivos extremos (exhausted, furious, freezing) van con adverbios como 'utterly', 'absolutely' o 'completely', no con 'very'.

wrong.very: 'very' va con adjetivos graduables (very tired), no con extremos como 'exhausted'.
wrong.fairly: 'fairly' (bastante) solo va con adjetivos graduables; con 'exhausted' es incorrecto.
wrong.slightly: 'slightly' (un poco) no combina con un adjetivo extremo como 'exhausted'.

examples: I'm utterly exhausted after that meeting.
She was very tired, but not exhausted.

prompt: Take a warm coat: it's ___ freezing outside!

explanation.rule: 'Freezing' es un adjetivo extremo (helado); se intensifica con 'absolutely' o 'really', no con 'very'.

wrong.very: 'very' no se usa con adjetivos extremos; se dice 'very cold' pero 'absolutely freezing'.
wrong.a bit: 'a bit' suaviza adjetivos graduables (a bit cold); con 'freezing' es contradictorio.
wrong.fairly: 'fairly' solo va con adjetivos graduables (fairly cold).

examples: It's absolutely freezing in this office.
The water was really freezing.

prompt: Which sentence is NOT correct in standard English?

explanation.rule: 'Furious' es un adjetivo extremo: no admite 'very'. Sí admite 'absolutely' o 'really'.

Es correcta: 'absolutely' es el adverbio típico con adjetivos extremos.
Es correcta: 'angry' es graduable y admite 'very'.
Es correcta: 'really' combina tanto con adjetivos graduables como con extremos.

examples: My boss was absolutely furious about the delay.
I was really angry with myself.

prompt: The view from the top of the mountain was absolutely ___.

explanation.rule: 'Absolutely' solo intensifica adjetivos extremos como 'stunning' (impresionante), 'amazing' o 'terrible'.

wrong.nice: 'nice' es un adjetivo graduable; 'absolutely nice' no es natural (se dice 'very nice').
wrong.pretty: 'pretty' es graduable; con 'absolutely' no es natural (se dice 'very pretty').
wrong.interesting: 'interesting' es graduable; se dice 'very interesting', no 'absolutely interesting'.

examples: The scenery was absolutely stunning.
The food was absolutely delicious.

prompt: Which adjective is the extreme form of 'hungry'?

explanation.rule: 'Starving' = muerto de hambre; es la forma extrema de 'hungry' y va con 'absolutely' o 'completely'.

wrong.greedy: 'greedy' es glotón o codicioso; describe un defecto, no tener mucha hambre.
wrong.famine: 'famine' es un sustantivo (hambruna), no un adjetivo.
wrong.appetising: 'appetising' describe comida que da hambre (apetitosa), no a una persona hambrienta.

examples: I'm absolutely starving: what's for dinner?
We were starving after the long walk.
